run.title: Exchange your first routes.
run.label: Local lab
run.body: Build Ze, start two peers on one Linux host, and inspect the route each receives. The tutorial includes the configuration, verification and cleanup.
run.success: Both sessions establish and each peer receives the other peer’s advertised prefix.

run.title: Try an existing configuration.
run.label: ExaBGP migration
run.body: Convert an ExaBGP configuration, review the result, and use the compatibility bridge for process scripts. The guide explains the limits and cutover checks.
run.success: Validate the converted configuration and verify your sessions and script behavior in a lab.

run.title: Keep your existing host.
run.label: Linux or Docker
run.body: Install the Linux service or build the Docker deployment image with persistent storage. The guides cover authenticated management, updates and removal; the Linux host keeps its existing interface configuration.
run.success: Connect to authenticated management and check that your configuration survives the documented restart or container recreation.

run.title: Give Ze its own system.
run.label: VM or appliance
run.body: Build an immutable gokrazy system for QEMU, Proxmox or hardware, with a read-only root and persistent configuration. The guide covers ISO installation, authenticated SSH, updates and previous-slot recovery.
run.success: Source builds produce disk images and installer ISOs. No public image release is available yet.

who.title: Route server
who.label: IXP
who.body: IXP operators can run the route-server lab first and compare policy behaviour before touching members.

who.title: Lab router
who.label: Lab
who.body: Network builders can bring up two BGP peers, inspect routes, and check whether Ze's operator tools fit their workflow.

who.title: ExaBGP replacement
who.label: Migration
who.body: ExaBGP users can try the migrator against an existing config and see which process scripts still translate cleanly.

who.title: White-box appliance
who.label: Appliance
who.body: People with spare x86 hardware can boot the appliance image and test the same configuration model without a general-purpose shell.

who.title: Looking glass
who.label: Observe
who.body: Operators who need read-only BGP visibility can publish a looking glass and inspect routes without giving shell access.

who.title: Protocol testbed
who.label: Interop
who.body: Protocol implementers can run Docker interop scenarios against FRR, BIRD, and GoBGP, then turn a failure into a test case.

who.title: AI-assisted operations
who.label: MCP
who.body: MCP exposes Ze commands and structured output to AI tools without a separate command set.
